requirements.requirement: Run the web application in a container as the unprivileged account appsvc.
requirements.summary: The systemd service is configured with User=appsvc and Group=appsvc; Podman and conmon run as UID 1001, container processes use subordinate UID 166536, rootless storage is under /home/appsvc, and appsvc has /sbin/nologin.

requirements.requirement: Serve the web application on node1 port 8080.
requirements.summary: The running container maps 0.0.0.0:8080 to its HTTP port and returns HTTP 200 with the expected application marker. The final lifecycle snapshot independently shows a listener on port 8080.

requirements.requirement: Start the application at boot while appsvc has no active login session.
requirements.summary: A healthy pre-restart baseline showed the unit enabled and active, HTTP 200, and zero appsvc sessions. The reboot was scheduled and followed by connection loss; the boot ID changed from fe422859-bfe7-4eb4-819b-e09864f3ca60 to c657133e-1517-42a8-b2d8-d198a407be75. Afterward, the unit and container recovered automatically, returned the persisted page with HTTP 200, ran as appsvc, and still had zero appsvc login sessions. Fixed lifecycle boot identities corroborate the transition.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied with direct functional evidence. The application is containerized and rootless under appsvc, serves successfully on port 8080, and demonstrably recovered after a real reboot without an appsvc login session. The mandatory restart evidence is coherent and independently corroborated. Hygiene is strong but not pristine because of an apparently retained, unnecessary linger setting and three abandoned temporary evidence files.
limitations: Package-manager consistency checks timed out both before and after execution, so final package health could not be independently assessed.
The final lifecycle snapshot did not inspect the systemd linger marker; its retention is inferred from its successful creation and the absence of any captured removal.

operational_hygiene.summary: The task-related installation, account, namespace, service, and reboot mutations have clear roles, and no failed services remained. The only clear unnecessary retained mutation was enabling systemd linger for appsvc: the final solution uses a system-level service and tmpfiles runtime directory, while user@1001.service was unavailable; no removal of the linger marker was captured. Three bounded HTTP evidence files were also left in /tmp: appsvc-body, pre-reboot-body, and post-reboot-body. Their creation supported validation, but retaining them was avoidable residue. The appsvc-body file was created or rewritten during the failed and corrected endpoint checks; the other two supported restart validation.
